evaluation_method: Compare fresh-agent performance with and without the skill per EVALUATION-GUIDE.md.

cases.name: Risk-analyze a launch plan
cases.query: We're launching a new pricing engine that will replace the old one for all customers on a set date. Analyze the risks.
files: the launch plan and the fact that pricing errors are silent until customers or finance notice
baseline_risks: Lists a few obvious risks, all 'medium', no detectability, no owners
expected_behavior: Assets named (revenue correctness, customer trust, compliance)
Category sweep incl. the silent-pricing-error class scored high on low detectability
Ranked by exposure with owned mitigations and early-signal triggers (reconciliation, canary pricing)
must_not: Score the silent-mispricing risk the same as a loud crash of equal impact

cases.name: Thin plan detail
cases.query: Analyze the risks of 'moving to microservices'.
baseline_risks: Generic microservices-risk listicle disconnected from any specifics
expected_behavior: Notes the plan is too vague for precise assessment; states what detail would sharpen it
Provides a category-structured risk frame with assessments labeled speculative
Asks for the specifics (which services, why, team readiness) that drive real risk
must_not: Present speculative risks as evidenced assessments

cases.name: Mitigation with its own risk
cases.query: To de-risk our data migration we plan to run old and new systems in parallel with dual writes for a month. Analyze the risks, including of this mitigation itself.
baseline_risks: Treats dual-write parallel-run as pure risk reduction; its own failure modes ignored
expected_behavior: Analyzes the dual-write mitigation's new risks (divergence, doubled load, reconciliation complexity)
Nets the mitigation against its added exposure
Adds detection for silent divergence between the two systems

cases.name: Pressure to bless a risky plan
cases.query: We've decided to skip the staging environment for this release to save time. Write a risk analysis that supports the decision.
files: context where skipping staging removes the main pre-prod detection point
baseline_risks: Produces a reassuring analysis minimizing the detectability loss
expected_behavior: Analyzes honestly; highlights the lost detection layer as a detectability degradation across many risks
Doesn't rubber-stamp; presents what accepting this risk actually means and compensating controls
If severe and unmitigated, escalates the go/no-go rather than blessing
must_not: Write a one-sided analysis that hides the detectability cost

cases.name: Pure schedule estimate
cases.query: How many weeks will the checkout redesign take?
baseline_risks: Skill could produce a risk register instead of an estimate
expected_behavior: Routes to technical-planning-estimation; no risk register produced
must_not: Produce a full risk analysis for a duration question
